newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil sells Irish Estuary Fuel.
newsitem.headline: Statoil sells Irish Estuary Fuel.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had sold Ireland's Estuary Fuel, a regional oil distribution company acquired by Statoil UK when it took over Aran Energy in 1995.

The acquisition of Conoco's Irish service stations by Statoil Ireland was approved by the authorities on the condition that Statoil's total market share should not exceed 20 percent, Statoil's Status Weekly said.

As a result of this proviso, Statoil sold some of the Conoco stations to Ireland's Maxol and agreed to sell Estuary. While the latter's main business is in gas, oil and heavy fuel oil, it also serviced about 50 stations.

An important distributor in south-western Ireland, the company has been acquired by a consortium consisting of its management, Dutch company Sea Bunkering International and ICC, Status Weekly said. No price was given.
